name: Urban Suite - Recycling
miniText: The scientific question is whether resource-restoring behavior can persist against faster but destructive exploitation. In NetLogo's Urban Suite - Recycling model, recyclers take partial resources or restore wasted cells, while wasteful agents exhaust cells and all agents maintain energy budgets. The selected literature connects this mechanism to resource feedback and collective sustainability: shared-resource dilemmas contextualize individually profitable depletion [1]; institutional evidence challenges assumptions that depletion is inevitable [2]; resource-use research connects management choices with longer-term sustainability [3]. Arbitrary gains, restoration costs and regeneration multipliers stand in for complex material cycles; neither label measures a real households environmental impact. The original NetLogo behavior is the baseline for reimplementation. This simulation offers a controlled thought experiment, and agreement with its output does not establish empirical validation.

modelSource.scientificOrigin: The original version of this model was developed during the Sprawl/Swarm Class at Illinois Institute of Technology in Fall 2006 under the supervision of Sarah Dunn and Martin Felsen, by the following students: Anita Phetkhamphou and Tidza Causevic . See http://www.sprawlcity.us/ for more information about this course. Further modifications and refinements were made by members of the Center for Connected Learning and Computer-Based Modeling before releasing it as an Urban Suite model. The Urban Suite models were developed as part of the Procedural Modeling of Cities project, under the sponsorship of NSF ITR award 0326542, Electronic Arts & Maxis. Please see the project web site ( http://ccl.northwestern.edu/cities/ ) for more information.
modelSource.notes: This is source research, not runtime execution or approval of the City Library reimplementation. Original model notices remain in the retained source.
